Planning your support

Finding the right page

Start with the kind of help you need

If an old link brought you here, you can still reach the website’s main service pages from the navigation above. Start with Services if you know the task but are unsure which service name fits it. The service directory separates administration, customer support, sales, content, research, bookkeeping and technical work. Choose the closest match and read the scope before deciding what you need. A missing page address does not mean that a particular service has been discontinued. Ask us when the task you had in mind is not clear from the directory.

Find help with inboxes and calendars

Open Admin support for email organisation, meeting coordination, reminders and recurring administrative tasks. Think about the requests that arrive each day and the decisions you still want to make yourself. The page explains examples of work that can be prepared for review and what information helps an assistant begin. If your original link referred to an executive assistant or scheduling support, this is a useful place to continue. You do not need to have every instruction written before making a first enquiry; one ordinary example can help explain the work.

Find customer service support

The Customer support page covers routine enquiries, approved responses and the tracking of requests that need a decision. Use it when customers are waiting for updates or when the same issue arrives through several channels. The important starting points are the policy the assistant should follow, the system where the conversation is recorded and the person who approves an exception. If an earlier link mentioned a help desk, live chat or service queue, this page can help you understand the relevant scope before contacting us.

Find sales and CRM help

Go to Sales and CRM for support with contact records, lead information, follow-ups and agreed sales administration. A useful enquiry describes which records need attention and how your team decides who should act next. The page also explains why changes such as deleting or merging records need a separate approval rule. If you arrived from a link about lead operations or CRM cleanup, you can continue there. Be clear about whether you want research, record maintenance or follow-up coordination, because each task has a different finished result.

Find bookkeeping information

Open Bookkeeping for information about invoices, transaction records, bank reconciliations and month-end preparation. Describe the accounting system, the period involved and the records you want organised. Financial approvals stay with the responsible person on your team. The service page explains the difference between preparing records and making decisions such as approving payments or accounting treatment. If your original link concerned accounts payable, receivables or a reconciliation task, this page is the relevant place to continue. Please keep private financial documents out of an initial general enquiry.

Find content and publishing support

Use Marketing and content when you need help organising briefs, approved assets, publishing dates and review steps. Start with the channel, audience and kind of material involved. If the work also includes updating a website, the WordPress or website service pages may be relevant. The distinction is useful: preparing a piece of content, approving its message and publishing the final version can be separate tasks. An old link about social media coordination or campaign administration can therefore lead to more than one suitable service page.

Find research or data support

The Research and data page explains support with information gathering, comparisons, record updates and agreed cleanup work. Tell us the question you want answered or the fields that need attention. A useful result might be a sourced comparison, a checked list or a clearly documented set of changes. Avoid asking for more information than the task needs, particularly when records concern other people. If the missing link mentioned a research brief, data entry or record checking, this page provides a sensible starting point for a new conversation.

Find website and technical services

Open Website services for planned website work, or use the full Services directory to find WordPress support, mobile app development and workflow automation. Explain whether you need a small update, a new feature or a larger build. The relevant pages describe how to agree a preview, review the result and decide what happens before a release. A missing marketing-page address does not give anyone permission to change your live site. Publishing, account access and other important actions still need the approval arrangements agreed for the work.

Choose an industry example

The Industries directory shows how support changes between businesses such as online stores, professional practices, agencies, real estate teams and technology companies. These pages are examples of working arrangements, rather than a requirement to fit one exact category. Choose the closest situation and compare the tasks with the service directory. If your business works across several sectors, describe the actual task and the people who review it. The same administrative skill may be used in different settings, while permissions and specialist decisions remain specific to your organisation.

Understand the working process

Go to How it works to read about preparing a task, agreeing the scope and reviewing the first results. This is useful when you know you need help but are unsure what a first request should contain. The page describes who provides instructions, who performs the agreed work and who approves decisions. You can start by describing an ordinary task and an example that needs extra attention. If the original link referred to onboarding or a working arrangement, this process page is a useful place to continue.

Discuss your support needs

Use the Contact page to describe the support you need. Share the recurring task, your current tools, expected workload and the result you want to review. You can begin with a normal example and explain what changes on a busy day. If a request needs someone else’s approval, name the responsible role and the decision involved. A short description is enough for a first conversation. The team can then discuss the scope, coverage and next steps with you. If an old link brought you here, include that address so we can help you find the right information.

Read about access and privacy

The Trust and security page explains questions to consider before sharing systems or records. The Privacy Policy explains information shared through enquiries and agreed work. These pages address different parts of the relationship. Reading a service description does not itself authorise access to a business account, and a general enquiry should not contain account passwords. If you reached this page while looking for data-handling information, use those two links and contact us about any particular statement you need clarified before sharing a sample.

Check a copied or saved address

A website address can stop working if a page was renamed, a link was copied incompletely or punctuation was added to its end. Check that the address belongs to assistlaneglobal.com and does not include text from the surrounding message. You can use the homepage rather than guessing a series of page names. If a bookmark is old, save the address of the page you find through the current navigation. Avoid changing account settings or entering information into a different website just because an unfamiliar page says it can repair the link.

Keep a useful reference when reporting the problem

If a link on this website brought you here, tell us which page you were reading and which link you selected. Include the missing address if you can copy it safely. A brief description of the topic is also useful, especially when the link came from an older email or document. Do not include private browser history, login details or unrelated screenshots. The aim is to identify the missing destination and guide you to the right information. You can continue browsing the current service and company pages while the link is being checked.
